Consider either (a) not creating/updating `assignee_notifications` entries when `notify_slack` is false (except for first-run bootstrap), or (b) explicitly recording a separate pending/disabled marker so a later run can still send the initial notification.

If a PR run hits `transient-failure`/`unknown` (or otherwise lacks facts), this will wipe `assignee_notifications` and can cause the next successful run to re-send an “initial” notification even if it was already sent before. Consider preserving the previous per-PR state when `returncode != 0` (or for `side` in `transient-failure`/`unknown`) so transient data fetch errors don’t reset notification history.

threads.body: `try_send_slack_notification()` returns `False` (and upstream marks `notification_pending`) for non-recoverable configuration problems like a missing webhook URL or missing user mapping. This will cause repeated attempts and repeated warnings on every run for the same assignee/PR until configuration is fixed, which can create noisy logs and unnecessary work. Consider making the send result tri-state (e.g., sent / retryable-failure / non-retryable-skip) so missing `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` or missing user mapping can be recorded as “skipped” (no retry) while transient network/Slack failures remain retryable; alternatively store a `disabled_reason` and/or `last_attempted_at` and throttle retries for config-related failures.

replies.body: Fixed. Slack send results are now tri-state: sent, retryable failure, or non-retryable skip. Missing `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` and missing user mappings are recorded as skipped instead of pending, while webhook/network errors still leave the notification pending for retry.

Simplified this further after discussion: instead of tracking non-retryable skip states, Slack notifications now fail fast for missing `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`, invalid `SLACK_USER_MAP_JSON`, or missing assignee mappings. The raised errors include the env var or PR/assignee needed to fix the configuration, and successful sends remain the only path that clears pending state.

threads.body: The Slack webhook error reporting is likely to be low-signal for HTTP failures: `HTTPError` (a `URLError` subclass) contains a response body that often includes Slack’s specific error (e.g., `invalid_payload`, `invalid_token`), but the current code discards it and raises `Slack webhook request failed: HTTP Error 400: Bad Request`. Catch `urllib.error.HTTPError` separately and include status code + response body (safely decoded) in the raised `RuntimeError` to make failures actionable.

+    return notification_state_from_body(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

+def notification_state_marker(state: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    stored_state = {k: v for k, v in state.items() if not k.startswith("_")}
+    state_json = json.dumps(stored_state, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
+    return f"<!-- pr-review-dashboard-state:{state_json} -->"
+

+    stripped = NOTIFICATION_STATE_MARKER_RE.sub("", md).rstrip()
+    return f"{stripped}\n\n{notification_state_marker(state)}\n"
